summary: Hayden Hill lookout: site set aside 1912, cab built 1940 to a Region 5 plan; only the cab went to the Bieber museum, and the move date is not in the sources.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin on a 10 foot enclosed timber tower (NHLR)
facts.status_note: Only the cab was reassembled at the Big Valley Museum grounds in Bieber; the register says the tower was not reassembled there

staffing.status: lookout station in use in the 1940s; in operation in March 1991; no later staffing reported

facts.agency: Modoc National Forest (original site); Big Valley Historical Museum (cab today)

events.note: Site set aside for administrative use (register: withdrawn; Forest Lookouts: approved)
Register says a structure stood by 1915; a June 1915 newspaper item mentions the Forest Service lookout peak
July 1923 item mentions a visit to the new lookout house on Hayden Hill; not reconciled with the register's 1940 date
Cab built to Region 5 Plan BC-301, per the register
July 1943 item refers to the Lookout Station at Hayden Hill
Supervisors approved moving the tower to the Bieber Museum grounds in March 1991; the move date is not in these sources; the register says only the cab was reassembled

evidence.supports: 1912 site set aside for administrative use
evidence.quote: 1912: Site was approved for administrative use.
The site was withdrawn for Administrative use in 1912 and structure stood by 1915.

evidence.supports: June 1915 item suggests travelers look over the country from the Forest Service lookout peak
evidence.quote: June 30, 1915: "In traveling to Adin you will do well to stop at the famous old mining camp at Hayden Hill and look over the country from the Forest Service lookout peak at this point." (New Era - Alturas)

evidence.supports: July 1923 visit to the new lookout house on Hayden Hill
evidence.quote: July 13, 1923: "The next day Susanville was reached via Adin and a visit paid to the new lookout house on Hayden Hill." (California District News Letter)

evidence.supports: cab constructed 1940 as Region 5 Plan BC-301 on a 10 foot enclosed timber tower
evidence.quote: Hayden Hill Lookout was constructed in 1940 and is described as a California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin on a 10 foot enclosed timber tower in both of Thornton's surveys.

evidence.supports: roof resembles another California plan; structure may be a hybrid
evidence.quote: The high peak roof is more reminiscent of the California Plan 4AR, so the structure may be a hybrid of some kind.

evidence.supports: 1991 newspaper calls the tower two-story and says it remains in operation
evidence.quote: The 2-story tower has been declared a historical site, according to Parks, even while it remains in operation.

evidence.supports: July 1943 item: man with mumps cared for by his wife at the Lookout Station at Hayden Hill
evidence.quote: July 1, 1943: "Reuban Lane is suffering with an attack of mumps. His wife is taking care of him at the Lookout Station at Hayden Hill." (Weekly Adin Argus)
1946: During the period of 1942 through 1946 this lookout made 13 first discoveries.

evidence.supports: March 1991 supervisors approved moving the tower to the Bieber Museum grounds
evidence.quote: March 19, 1991: "The supervisors last week approved a request from museum board member Carl Parks to relocate the Hayden Hill fire lookout tower from its present site to the Bieber Museum grounds."

evidence.supports: item attributed to the Lassen County Times
evidence.quote: "The supervisors unanimously approved Parks' request to relocate the tower." (Lassen County Times)

evidence.supports: a new tower had to be built first so coverage would not lapse
evidence.quote: Before that can take place, however, a new tower must be built and made operational, since there cannot by law be a lapse in coverage of the area.

evidence.supports: Amax Gold was to handle dismantling, relocating and reassembly
evidence.quote: Amax Gold, whose Lassen Gold Mining subsidiary is currently in the midst of developing the Hayden Hill area, will take care of the actual dismantling, relocating, and reassembling of the tower.

evidence.supports: only the cab, not the tower, was reassembled at the museum and stands today
evidence.quote: The cabin, but not the tower has been reassembled at the Museum and stands today.

evidence.supports: administered by the Big Valley Historical Museum
evidence.quote: Administered by Big Valley Historical Museum - Bieber, California

evidence.supports: registered on the NHLR on October 30, 2019

resolved_conflicts.field: cab build date (1923 item vs 1940 register date)
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not reconciled. The story reports the 1923 'new lookout house' mention and the register's 1940 date side by side; the events list keeps 1940 as the register's build date.

resolved_conflicts.field: tower height and form (10 foot enclosed tower vs 2-story tower)
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The story uses the register's description and notes that the 1991 newspaper called the tower two-story.

notes_for_editor: Two sources read: the NHLR page and the Forest Lookouts page. No source read describes what remains at the original Hayden Hill site today. The record's location (ffla 40.99793, -120.87038) differs from west_us_lookouts by about 923 m; not resolved. The academia.edu figure seen in search (1940 cab relocated to the Big Valley Historical Museum) returned HTTP 403, so it is not cited. The museum's Facebook page was not readable. The move date and the museum's visiting hours are not in the sources read. Story runs about 340 words including footnotes.
